nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be linear orders, let $f : \alpha \to \beta$ be monotone, and let $n$ be a natural number. For all wires $i, j \in \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ and every assignment $v$ of a value in $\alpha$ to each wire, the comparator $(i, j)$ applied to $f \circ v$ gives $f \circ w$, where $w$ is the output of the comparator $(i, j)$ on $v$.
nodes.title: Comparators commute with monotone maps

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linear order and let $n$ be a natural number. For all wires $i, j \in \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ and every assignment $v$ of a value in $\alpha$ to each wire, there is a permutation $\sigma$ of the wires such that the output of the comparator $(i, j)$ on $v$ is $v \circ \sigma$.
nodes.title: A comparator permutes its inputs

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linear order, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $v$ assign a value $v(k) \in \alpha$ to each wire $k \in \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$. For wires $i$ and $j$, the comparator $(i, j)$ sends $v$ to the assignment that has $\min(v(i), v(j))$ on wire $i$, $\max(v(i), v(j))$ on wire $j$ when $j \ne i$, and $v(k)$ on every other wire $k$.
nodes.title: Comparator

nodes.summary: For every Boolean input $v$ on $n$ wires, applying the threshold map that sends a natural number $k$ to true if $n \le k$ and to false otherwise to the spread of $v$ gives back $v$: for every wire $i$, the spread of $v$ at $i$ is at least $n$ exactly when $v(i)$ is true.
nodes.title: A Boolean input is a threshold of its spread

nodes.summary: A comparator network on $n$ wires is a finite list of pairs $(i, j)$ of wires $i, j \in \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, each pair standing for the comparator $(i, j)$; the comparators are applied in list order.
nodes.title: Comparator network

nodes.summary: For an injective map $w$ from $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ to the natural numbers, the ranking permutation of $w$ is the permutation of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that sends each $i$ to the rank of $w(i)$ among the values of $w$, that is, to the number of indices $j$ with $w(j) < w(i)$. Since $w$ is injective, this map is a bijection.
nodes.title: The ranking permutation

nodes.summary: For a map $w$ from $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ to the natural numbers and an index $i < n$, the rank of $w(i)$ among the values of $w$ is the number of indices $j < n$ with $w(j) < w(i)$. It is less than $n$, so it is again an index in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.
nodes.title: Rank among the values of an input

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be linear orders and let $f : \alpha \to \beta$ be monotone. For every comparator network on $n$ wires and every assignment $v$ of a value in $\alpha$ to each wire, the output of the network on $f \circ v$ is $f \circ w$, where $w$ is the output of the network on $v$.
nodes.title: Networks commute with monotone maps

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linear order. For every comparator network on $n$ wires and every assignment $v$ of a value in $\alpha$ to each wire, there is a permutation $\sigma$ of the wires such that the output of the network on $v$ is $v \circ \sigma$.
nodes.title: The output of a comparator network is a permutation of its input

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linear order. The output of a comparator network on an assignment $v$ of a value in $\alpha$ to each of its $n$ wires is obtained by starting from $v$ and applying the comparators of the network one after another, in list order.
nodes.title: Running a comparator network

nodes.summary: A comparator network passes the Boolean sorting test if and only if it sorts inputs over the Booleans, that is, for every assignment of a Boolean value to each wire, the output of the network is monotone in the wire order.
nodes.title: The Boolean sorting test is correct

nodes.summary: The Boolean sorting test of a comparator network on $n$ wires returns true exactly when, for every assignment $v$ of a Boolean value to each wire, the output $w$ of the network on $v$ satisfies $w(i) \le w(j)$ for all wires $i \le j$, where $\mathrm{false} < \mathrm{true}$.
nodes.title: Boolean sorting test

nodes.summary: If a comparator network on $n$ wires passes the Boolean sorting test, then for every linear order $\alpha$ it sorts inputs over $\alpha$: for every assignment $v$ of a value in $\alpha$ to each wire, the output of the network on $v$ is monotone in the wire order.
nodes.title: A network that passes the Boolean sorting test sorts over every linear order

nodes.summary: The 0-1 principle (CLRS Theorem 27.2): a network that sorts every Boolean input sorts every input over every linear order.
nodes.title: The 0-1 principle

nodes.summary: A network that sorts every input with distinct natural values sorts every input over every linear order.
nodes.title: Sorting distinct inputs suffices

nodes.summary: A comparator network on $n$ wires that sorts each of the $n!$ permutations $\sigma$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, viewed as the input whose value on wire $i$ is $\sigma(i)$, sorts every input over every linear order.
nodes.title: The permutation principle

nodes.summary: A comparator network on $n$ wires sorts inputs over a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ if, for every input $v$ assigning a value in $\alpha$ to each wire, the output of running the network on $v$ is monotone in the wire order: for all wires $i \le j$, the output value on wire $i$ is at most the output value on wire $j$.
nodes.title: Networks that sort

nodes.summary: For a Boolean input $v$ on $n$ wires, the spread of $v$ is the input with natural-number values whose value on wire $i < n$ is $n + i$ if $v(i)$ is true and $i$ if $v(i)$ is false.
nodes.title: Spread of a Boolean input
